title: Degree-one derived classes classify short exact extensions
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] with derived category $D(\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and let $P,Q\in\mathcal A$. Sending a short exact sequence $0\to P\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{v}Q\to0$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] to its connecting morphism $Q[0]\to P[0][1]$ is a bijection from isomorphism classes of such sequences to $\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal A}(Q,P)$ [def-pc-ext]. Here two sequences are isomorphic precisely when there is an isomorphism $h:B\to B'$ satisfying $h\circ u=u'$ and $v'\circ h=v$, so that the endpoint maps are identities. For any exact additive functor $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ to another abelian category with derived category, the class of the image short exact sequence is the image of its class under the termwise derived functor $D(F)$.

source.place: Tag 06XV, lemma-ext-1; Tag 06XU, lemma-yoneda-extension, with degree-one equivalence of extensions. Exact-functor compatibility follows by applying the termwise exact functor to the single-complex triangle; Mathlib Ext.mapExactFunctor_extClass covers this compatibility alone.

proof.text: The single functor is fully faithful. For n < 0, Hom(S(X), S(Y)[n]) vanishes by standard t-structure orthogonality: S(X) is <= 0 and S(Y)[n] is >= -n > 0. This is the private Lean lemma single_shift_negative_zero.

For a distinguished triangle S(P) -> S(B) -> S(Q) -> S(P)[1], the negative-shift vanishing and full faithfulness identify the first map as a kernel of the second, and the second as a cokernel of the first. Indeed Hom exactness gives existence of each factorization; uniqueness follows by applying the preceding negative-shift vanishing to the adjacent shifted endpoint. Mathlib AbelianSubcategory.isLimitKernelForkOfDistTriang and isColimitCokernelCoforkOfDistTriang package exactly these universal properties. The first arrow is mono, the second epi, and the kernel property gives exactness. This is shortExact_of_single_triangle, so no equivalence with an independently constructed abelian heart is needed.

For two distinguished triangles with the same single terms and first two maps, TR3 with identities on the first two terms gives c on the third with b;c=b and delta=c;deltaPrime. Hom(-,S(Q)) exactness gives c-id=delta;w. Since S(P)[1] is <= -1 and S(Q) is >= 0, w=0 by orthogonality; thus c=id and the boundaries agree. This is the proved private lemma single_triangle_boundary_unique.

Given an Ext-one class xi, use its derived Hom representative and distinguished_cocone_triangle₂ (TR1 and inverse rotation) to obtain S(P) -> M -> S(Q) with boundary exactly xi.hom. Standard t-structure extension closure (Mathlib isLE₂ and isGE₂, proved from Hom exactness and orthogonality) puts M in degree zero. Concentration gives e:M≅S(B). Lift f;e.hom and e.inv;g through the fully faithful single functor to a and b. Faithfulness and the triangle zero-composite give a;b=0. Transport the triangle along identities and e to single terms. Step 2 makes the lifted complex short exact; its canonical single triangle from the short-exact-complex construction has boundary equal to xi.hom by step 3. Ext.homEquiv injectivity yields h.extClass=xi.

If two short exact complexes have equal Ext classes, their single triangles have equal boundaries by extClass_hom. complete_distinguished_triangle_morphism₂ (TR3 after rotation) completes the identities on the first and third objects to a triangle map. Its middle component is an isomorphism by the two-isomorphisms criterion. The fully faithful single functor lifts this isomorphism to B≅BPrime and faithfulness gives a;e.hom=aPrime and e.hom;bPrime=b. Conversely an endpoint-identity isomorphism defines a morphism of short complexes; extClass_naturality reduces to equality because both endpoint maps are identities.

For every exact additive functor F, apply Mathlib Abelian.Ext.mapExactFunctor_extClass F h. This is the single-triangle exact-functor comparison expressed through Ext.homEquiv and includes the endpoint and shift comparisons. It is precisely the third clause.

lean.statement: theorem ext_one_extension_classification {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C] [HasDerivedCategory.{t} C] [HasExt.{w} C] (P Q : C) : (∀ ξ : Abelian.Ext Q P 1, ∃ (B : C) (a : P ⟶ B) (b : B ⟶ Q) (z : a ≫ b = 0) (h : (ShortComplex.mk a b z).ShortExact), h.extClass = ξ) ∧ (∀ (B B' : C) (a : P ⟶ B) (b : B ⟶ Q) (z : a ≫ b = 0) (h : (ShortComplex.mk a b z).ShortExact) (a' : P ⟶ B') (b' : B' ⟶ Q) (z' : a' ≫ b' = 0) (h' : (ShortComplex.mk a' b' z').ShortExact), h.extClass = h'.extClass ↔ ∃ e : B ≅ B', a ≫ e.hom = a' ∧ e.hom ≫ b' = b) ∧ (∀ (D : Type u') [Category.{v'} D] [Abelian D] [HasDerivedCategory.{t'} D] [HasExt.{w'} D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F] (B : C) (a : P ⟶ B) (b : B ⟶ Q) (z : a ≫ b = 0) (h : (ShortComplex.mk a b z).ShortExact), h.extClass.mapExactFunctor F = (h.map_of_exact F).extClass)
